Title: Recursive source walk and diff
Detail: Walks SourcePath recursively writing one manifest row per file (SR-001); Compare-SourceToBackup returns the pure NewOrChanged/RemovedFromSource diff consumed by the run.

Title: xxHash128 file hashing
Detail: Streams the file through System.IO.Hashing.XxHash128 and formats big-endian bytes as 32-char uppercase hex (SR-002); Initialize-XxHashLibrary guarantees the type is loaded.

Title: Content-addressed dedup keying
Detail: Groups source rows by (xxH2Hash,Length) and copies the physical data once per key (SR-003); Get-HashSizeFileName derives the content-addressed name; later names flagged Duplicate.

Title: Extension-gated 7-Zip storage
Detail: Test-ShouldCompress decides by extension only (SR-004); Compress-FileWithSevenZip writes a .7z whose extension is appended to the stored name so Compressed and filename agree.

Title: Dated snapshot completion
Detail: Builds the snapshot in Temp staging then, when the manifest state changed (Compare-SourceToBackup diff non-empty — NOT the physical-copy counter, which misses dedup-served adds and shared-content removals), renames it to Snapshot_<prior-backup-date> after its manifest is written (SR-005); no snapshot for a manifest-identical run or the latest/live state; same-second disambiguator preserved. An optional -BackupTime seam (cf. Test-HashRecalcDue -Now) dates the snapshot deterministically for tests.

Title: Refcount-aware eviction
Detail: Evicts a removed file's data to staging only when no surviving manifest row references its (hash,size) (SR-006); shared data is retained (B9).

Title: Restore-kit deposition
Detail: Copies Reconstruct.ps1, reconstruct.sh, FileBackup.Common.psm1, System.IO.Hashing.dll, RECONSTRUCT.paths.json and RECONSTRUCT.bat into the live backup and each dated snapshot (SR-007). Common imports nothing from Engine (load-bearing split).

Title: Standalone reconstruction
Detail: Rebuilds the tree from the manifest using bundled Common (SR-008); decompresses .7z rows via Expand-FileWithSevenZip and recovers blank-DataPath rows by scanning for a content-hash match.

Title: Restore target guard
Detail: Rejects a restore target located inside the backup folder before writing any file, and refuses any manifest row whose canonicalized destination falls outside the target root — the row is warned, counted unrestored, and fails the run per SR-029 (SR-009).

Title: Point-in-time restore authority
Detail: When launched from a Snapshot_<date> folder, uses that snapshot's own manifest as the sole authority (no newer-manifest overlay) and resolves bytes by (xxH2Hash,Length) via Find-DataFileByHash over the data pool = backup root + all snapshot folders (SR-010). The scan's infrastructure-name skip is root-level only per SR-022 (a nested infra-named file is data and a legitimate recovery source, B6); matching is by (hash,length) — the skip is an optimization, not a correctness gate.

Title: Rehash scheduling decision
Detail: Test-HashRecalcDue maps A/E/D/W/M/Y/N + last-run + injectable -Now to a recalc boolean (SR-011); Get/Set-LastHashRun persist the timestamp in FileBackupState.json.

Title: Storage-layout migration
Detail: Re-lays-out existing data when PreserveFolderTree/compression change (SR-012), copying data and writing the new manifest before deleting old files (crash-safe B7).

Title: StoredAsHashSize bookkeeping
Detail: Sets/flips the StoredAsHashSize manifest column to match the active layout (SR-013) so restore resolves data filenames correctly.

Title: Per-set isolation and exit code
Detail: FileBackup.ps1 loops Invoke-BackupSet per set updating an OverallSuccess [ref] (SR-014); a set's failure is logged without aborting the loop and yields exit 1.

Title: Conditional non-fatal mail
Detail: Sends mail only when SMTP fields are present and -NoMail is unset (SR-015); Send-MailMessage failure is caught and logged WARN, never changing exit status (B15).

Title: Non-interactive automation path
Detail: -NonInteractive threads from FileBackup.ps1 through Initialize-Dependencies into Resolve-OptionalTool (degrade missing tool to absent) and Initialize-XxHashLibrary (-AutoInstall or throw with guidance) so an unattended run never blocks on a prompt (SR-016).

Title: Stale staging abort
Detail: Detects a pre-existing Temp staging folder under ChangePath and aborts with a message naming it (SR-017) rather than overwriting a half-written prior run.

Title: Missing-config guard
Detail: Tests ConfigPath with -PathType Leaf and throws "Config file not found" before any work (SR-018).

Title: External-tool resolution
Detail: Resolve-OptionalTool/Initialize-Dependencies locate configured tools; missing 7-Zip fails before any compression-enabled set is processed, while missing ffprobe leaves MediaMBPerSec blank (SR-020).

Title: Literal/bracket-safe paths
Detail: All file ops use -LiteralPath and [System.IO.Path]::GetDirectoryName/GetFileName instead of Split-Path -LiteralPath -Parent/-Leaf (which throws on PS7), keeping Unicode/bracketed names intact (SR-021).

Title: Root-only infrastructure test
Detail: Classifies kit/manifest names as infrastructure only at the backup root (SR-022); nested same-named user files are data (B6). The allowlist covers every artifact New-ReconstructScript deploys, including the RECONSTRUCT.paths.json sidecar (2026-07-02 review).

Title: Restore capacity check
Detail: Sums required bytes using decompressed sizes for .7z rows and compares against target free space before restoring (SR-023, B10/B11).

Title: Deterministic manifest output
Detail: Stable row ordering + typed serialization make an unchanged re-run produce byte-identical manifest rows (SR-024).

Title: Manifest schema round-trip
Detail: Read/Write-Manifest are the only IO for the 9-column schema, preserving typed Length/LastWriteTime, tolerating null/empty, and returning @() for a missing file (SR-025).

Title: Cross-change duplicate collapse
Detail: After a run, collapses identical data shared across change folders to a single stored copy still resolvable from each (SR-026).

Title: Dated-snapshot storage and clean cutover
Detail: Persists each set's last backup-completion time in FileBackupState.json (new Get/Set-LastBackupRun) to date the next snapshot; snapshots keep the full pre-run manifest plus only superseded bytes (Move-RemovedFilesToStaging) deduped by Optimize-ChangeFolders; the ^Snapshot_ regex replaces ChangeFolderRegex in Get-FileBackupDefaults and engine/Reconstruct drop all Pre_*_Changes handling (SR-028). Set-LastBackupRun accepts an injectable -When for deterministic test timelines.

Title: Config builder and quick-start
Detail: CredSetEx.ps1 plus the README quick-start let a new user produce a valid CLIXML config and run a first backup (SR-027); System.IO.Hashing auto-installs on first use.

Title: Reconstruct unrestored-row accounting
Detail: The restore loop records every row it skips (blank-DataPath hash-recovery failure, missing DataPath, extraction failure) instead of silently continuing; after the loop a non-empty list logs an INCOMPLETE summary and throws, so a scripted pwsh -File caller exits non-zero (SR-029). A clean run keeps exit 0.

Title: Bash xxh128 wrapper
Detail: hash_file wraps xxhsum -H128 / xxh128sum, normalizing output to the 32-char uppercase big-endian hex Get-FileXxHash emits (SR-030). Lives inside the single self-contained reconstruct.sh (no sourced runtime libs, per plan pinned decision); the bottom-of-file main guard lets bats source the script to unit-test the function. Conformance pinned by golden fixtures under tests/fixtures/hash-conformance/.

Title: Bash standalone restorer
Detail: reconstruct.sh restores from the backup root or a Snapshot_<date> folder with the SR-031 semantics, mirroring Reconstruct.ps1: authority selection by the script's own folder name (^Snapshot_ regex), RFC-4180 manifest parse, RelativePath backslash-to-slash mapping, data-pool (backup root + all snapshots) hash recovery for blank/missing DataPath rows, 7z expansion of compressed rows, target-inside-backup guard, capacity pre-check, and unrestored-row accounting with a non-zero exit naming the count (mirrors SR-029). Single self-contained file; tool preflight fails loudly with remediation (SN-015 pattern).

Title: Manifest portability layer
Detail: parse_manifest does RFC-4180 CSV parsing via gawk FPAT (handles quoted fields with commas/embedded quotes) and tolerates a UTF-8 BOM; to_posix_path maps RelativePath backslashes to '/'; LastWriteTimeStr is treated as opaque ISO-8601 'O' text (never reparsed/reformatted). Both are functions inside the self-contained reconstruct.sh, unit-tested by sourcing it under bats (SR-032).

Title: Bash backup engine
Detail: Produces contract-conformant backups (manifest schema, dedup, short names via the shared alphabet, .7z gating, dated snapshots, refcount eviction) interoperable with the PowerShell engine (SR-033). Phase bash-v2 — decompose further before implementation.

Title: Container lifecycle workflow
Detail: Builds a digest-pinned non-root image, checksum-verifies the baked System.IO.Hashing package, runs a compressed backup from a read-only source using a separate writable source-state mount and byte-exact restore smoke test, exports docker-loadable tar archives, and tags/pushes/pulls fully-qualified OCI image references without accepting registry secrets as arguments.

Title: Run-state integrity gate
Detail: Invoke-BackupSet reads the prior backup date before any mutation and throws when it is null while the existing MANIFEST.csv still has rows, and an unparseable FileBackupState.json surfaces as a failure rather than an empty first-run state — so a non-initial run can never take the first-backup branch of Complete-ChangeFolder that discards staged history (SR-035).

Title: Empty-source refusal
Detail: When Update-SourceManifest returns zero rows for a source whose backup MANIFEST.csv still has rows, Invoke-BackupSet removes its staging folder and throws unless Set.AllowEmptySource is true; the error names the surviving row count and the override key (SR-036).

Title: Portable tool resolution
Detail: SevenZipDefaultPath is seeded from $env:FILEBACKUP_7ZIP_PATH (no module-scope Windows path construction); Initialize-Dependencies prefers the set's Tools.SevenZipPath, and the missing-7-Zip remediation names both knobs (SR-037).

Title: Witness sidecar writer
Detail: Write-Manifest writes MANIFEST.csv then calls Write-ManifestWitness, which computes Get-FileXxHash over the written file, emits Version/Rows/Bytes/XxH128/Written as UTF-8 (no BOM) LF key=value lines to MANIFEST.csv.meta.tmp in the same folder and publishes it with Move-Item -Force (atomic rename over any prior sidecar). Both helpers live in Common because Reconstruct.ps1 may call only Common (AGENTS.md sec.3, guarded by TC-048). WitnessFilename is added to Get-FileBackupDefaults and to Test-IsInfrastructureFile's root-level allowlist beside RECONSTRUCT.paths.json. Snapshots inherit their own witness because Complete-ChangeFolder rewrites the staging manifest through Write-Manifest before the rename; the sidecar is deliberately NOT added to the kit-artifact copy list (that would overwrite the snapshot's witness with the backup root's) (SR-038).

Title: Restore-side witness verification
Detail: Test-ManifestWitness (Common) parses MANIFEST.csv.meta, compares Bytes/Rows/XxH128 against the manifest on disk and returns a verdict object (Verified|Absent|Mismatch|Malformed) plus the failing field. Reconstruct.ps1 calls it inside Read-RawManifest's replacement, after the manifest-exists check and before the capacity pre-check, and adds the CSV header-shape check that bash already performs; bash/reconstruct.sh gains verify_manifest_witness (grep/cut key=value, wc via parse_manifest, xxh128sum) at the same point in main(), immediately after the existing header guard. Absent sidecar = WARN and continue unless -RequireWitness/--require-witness (SR-039).

Title: Restore exit-code taxonomy
Detail: Find-DataFileByHash returns [pscustomobject]@{Path;Cause;Detail} with Cause in Found|ContentMissing|DependencyMissing|StorageUnreadable|CandidateError (search folders are probed for existence/readability, an archive candidate met without a usable 7-Zip yields DependencyMissing, a caught extraction error yields CandidateError); the restore loop records {RelativePath;Cause;Detail} per unrestored row and the summary classifies them into the content class (exit 1) and the host class (exit 4). Exit-Reconstruct centralizes logging plus, under -ExitCode (passed by RECONSTRUCT.bat), 'exit <code>'; otherwise it throws, preserving the existing message wording so in-process callers and the harness keep working. reconstruct.sh keeps die()=2 and gains die_code() for 3 and the 1-vs-4 split at the end of main(); its usage text and header comment carry the table (SR-040).

Title: Move-loop failure aggregation
Detail: Both move loops take [ref]$OverallSuccess (as Invoke-BackupFileGroup already does), wrap the Move-Item plus its destination-directory creation in try/catch, and on failure log 'Failed to <evict|preserve> ...: <message>' at ERROR, add the entry to a local failure list, set OverallSuccess to false and continue; each returns/logs a summary count so a partially staged snapshot is explicit. Invoke-BackupSet passes the ref and proceeds to Complete-ChangeFolder so staging is never orphaned (SR-017) (SR-041).

Title: Validating configuration loader
Detail: Import-BackupConfiguration (exported from Engine, not Common — config loading is backup-only and Common must stay restore-safe) dispatches on the file extension, replacing FileBackup.ps1:100-125. The JSON branch parses with ConvertFrom-Json, requires an integer ConfigVersion within [1,$script:ConfigSchemaVersion], runs Assert-NoUnknownConfigKey over the top level, Tools, Secrets and each set (rejecting Secrets.Credential explicitly), then Test-BackupConfigurationShape; the CLIXML branch runs Test-BackupConfigurationShape only, preserving today's message wording so existing expectations hold. Type checks read the parsed JSON node's actual type — a quoted "false" is rejected rather than passed to [bool], which would coerce it true. Resolve-BackupSetDefaults materializes SourceStatePath=SourcePath and AllowEmptySource=$false and upper-cases HashRecalcFreq, so the engine's [bool] and ToUpperInvariant casts become belt-and-braces. Errors are terminating, single, first-in-document-order, and name the JSON path. container/FileBackup.schema.json is the published draft-07 mirror (additionalProperties:false) used for documentation and TC-077, not at runtime — keeping it out of the image and off the Dockerfile COPY list (SR-042).

Title: Entry-point status codes
Detail: FileBackup.ps1 gains [switch]$ExitCode and wraps the Import-BackupConfiguration call: on failure it writes the message to stderr and, when the switch is set, to the global log path before 'exit 2'; without the switch it rethrows so & $entry keeps throwing for tests/Unit/Engine.Tests.ps1 and the harness. The trailing 'if (-not $overallSuccess) { exit 1 }' is unchanged, so Coverage.Tests' exit-1 expectation (TC-034) holds in both modes. container/entrypoint.sh adds -ExitCode to the exec argument list ahead of "$@". The code meanings match WP1's restore table (0 complete / 1 incomplete / 2 usage-precondition) so one vocabulary covers both halves of IF-001 (SR-043).
